post.summary: One advisory search page (L1-ADP-16). Graph kinds `subject`, `resource`, `action`; management kinds `roles` and `role` (a role version with its computed "Not included" block, §8.17.9.2, E11), `admin-grant` (an admin Grant's meta-actions one by one, reserved ones apart), `holdings` (the viewer's own holdings, each a usable ADP `holding` basis, IA-5) and `changes` (information only, IA-2: an auditor sees every change, anyone else only those about them); `bulk-impact` (each Grant revoke of a bulk job and their sum, E17); `sources` (each live Acceptance by use with its blast radius, and the partners whose authority bridging Grants recognize up to their ceilings; §8.17.9.3, §5.13); developer kinds `schema-publications` (a namespace's published versions and where each stands here: there is no accept, a domain accepts only by its own `acceptance.amend` with the exact fingerprint, X21), `change-impact` (a role move or a `policy.set` candidate: abilities gained and lost per holder count, expansion requirements, orphan rows; X20, TN-121, §5.8; the SMT relation is `unknown` until proved), `revocation-impact` (subtree, staleness exposure, index lag, orphan tuples; §5.4) and `compromise-impact` (Exercises, Grants, contributions, projections and Claims in a window; SEC15). Developer kinds answer only the domain's auditors, and `revocation-impact` of a Grant also whoever stands above it in its lineage: the root of its Anchor or a holder of a Grant it derives from (XI-5); anyone else gets an empty page. `changes` also lists Grants whose agency names the reader and ingested regime key-events about the reader (`kind: key_event` with `class` and `issuer`; SI-21, SI-13, U26). Hub kinds `inventory` (holdings in the groups acting for you, shared from you and your authority, with the Anchors the reader roots) and `activity` (allowed uses by or for the reader; a DENY is not a use) answer only the reading Party about itself (XI-9, XI-22). The agent kind `agent-status` answers an agent Instance about itself only: whether it is live, its Mandate, and the Grants its Party holds with their actions, horizon and budget left; nothing about any other Party's delegations (A-11, E26). `outcome` (`{exercise, intent}`: what executors reported about one Exercise, compared with the allowed intent; only its actor Party, and a reporter for its own reports; OP-154 m.3 (u), E64, EI-10). `resource-incarnation` (`{namespace, path}`: the lifecycle facts domain products declared for one resource and its highest incarnation; the domain's auditors only; OP-156 m.3 (k), INV-32). `eligible-set` (`{gate_class, resource, digest}`: the named holders of `approve:<class>` now, as `eligibility:set` answers it; OP-156 m.3 (t), E41). `discovery` (`{unregistered?}`: each third-party application discovery connectors reported with `discovered_app` Claims, and the live agent or system Parties that account for it; only the unaccounted ones with `unregistered: true`; the domain's auditors only; AG-43, OP-156 m.4). Nothing is recorded.

200.description: `results`, `page` and `context.advisory: true`. A developer kind's results hold one report.

400.description: Not a search of this kind (a protocol error, L1-ADP-3).

503.description: No answer within the search deadline, never a partial list.

The publisher is the actor of the `check` AIS; a package whose authority-relevant parameter has no closed type is refused with its warnings and nothing is kept. A kept package changes no domain: each domain accepts only with its own reserved `acceptance.amend` naming the exact fingerprint, and there is no accept here, not even for a publisher who administers a target domain.

post.summary: Starts a Record Export: the body is the ADP request that committed the access.audit_export Exercise, with its AIS, and the authenticated PEP is the one its AIS names. A package streams at once as a CBOR sequence (export.cddl) read 10 000 records at a time with no limit on the range; with `stream: "mirror"` the answer names the Replica Mirror run. Billing, quota or plan state never closes it (anti-hostage k.2). It is the domain's record, apart from a person's data export (TN-79).

Problem.description: RFC 9457. `type` is `urn:suiss:access:problem:<code>`, or `about:blank` when the status says all.

reason.description: A stable, non-secret reason narrowing `code`, such as `signer-no-key` on a 503 while no operational key of the domain may sign (SAI-46, CR-23).

errors.description: The parts of the request a protocol problem is about (RFC 9457 §3); never request values.

pointer.description: A JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the request body, as a URI fragment, e.g. `#/set/basis`.

code.description: Stable code of what is wrong there.

actor_kind.description: The kind the Party's `party_register` recorded; nothing changes it (OP-149 m.8).

consistency_token.description: Opaque; the head the answer was read at.

AsOf.description: A ledger position in decimal, or an RFC 3339 time.

PartyId.description: PartyID, unpadded base64url of its 16 bytes (OP-149 m.16 (f)).

actor_kind.description: The kind the Party's `party_register` recorded; nothing changes it (OP-149 m.8).

consistency_token.description: Opaque; the head the answer was read at.

set.description: The context of an ADP `check` without `mode` and `nonce`: `domain`, `intent`, `basis`, `capacity`, `proofs` (L1-ADP-5…9).

as_of.description: A consistency token: answered at or after it (P36).

consistency_token.description: Opaque; the head the answer was read at.

tenant.description: Opaque tenant id (`tnt_…`), the same id events carry in `accesstenant`, `access_tenant` and `tenant` (OP-149 m.15 (i)).

realms.description: The tenant's live realms, by slug.

version.description: Changes exactly when the snapshot does.

retention.description: Retention policies (OP-147); empty until they are stored.

id.description: The realm, as events name it in `accessrealm` and `realm`.

issuer.description: The realm's fixed issuer; its `/.well-known/suiss-configuration` describes it.

webhooks.description: The Suiss webhook profile's delivery method: CloudEvents 1.0 structured JSON signed per Standard Webhooks.

realm.description: The realm, as the tenant snapshot names it.

client_id.description: The client whose pairwise `sub` is meant, its sector (MD-10): a client of the realm, e.g. Relay's client of it, when a PEP asks; the asking platform client itself when it asks with its assertion (OP-149 m.37; another value is 400 client-mismatch).

items.description: PartyID, base64url of 16 bytes.
A pairwise `sub` of the client, 43 characters.

party.description: PartyID, for a subject with a Party.

client_id.description: For a `sub` that is the pairwise pseudonym of a client of the realm without a Party (the `sub` of its service tokens), that client.

resolved.description: Each entry carries `sub` and exactly one of `party` and `client_id`.

unknown.description: The entries asked for that did not resolve, as given.

consistency_token.description: Opaque; the governing domain's head before the read.

status.description: Only allowed Exercises are recorded; others are not found.

intent.description: The intent digest it was allowed for.

instance.description: The actor InstanceID; absent for an anonymous actor.

payload.description: The receipt payload, dCBOR (`application/access-receipt+cbor`). The receipt is addressed to PEPs: a client certificate caller reads it; a platform client asking with its assertion reads the record without `receipt` (OP-149 m.37).

cose_sign1.description: The receipt as the decision point signed it, COSE_Sign1 under usage `receipt`.

key_excerpt.description: The binding-signed excerpt of the signing key (CR-58 m.1).

capacity.description: The capacity the actor declared: `own`, or `{for}` the PartyID it acted for.

agency.description: The chain from the principal to the agent; the agent of a link is the principal of the next. Empty when the actor acted for itself, or for another Party without a Mandate on its Instance.

mandate.description: The MandateID the agent acted under, 16 bytes.

payload.description: The receipt payload, dCBOR (`application/access-receipt+cbor`); its `agency` is the chain above.

cose_sign1.description: The receipt as the decision point signed it, COSE_Sign1 under usage `receipt`.

key_excerpt.description: The binding-signed excerpt of the signing key (CR-58 m.1).

items.description: A live realm of the tenant, as the tenant snapshot names it.

realms.description: The realms to pair with; every live realm of the tenant when absent (OP-149 m.16 (d)).

intent.description: Digest of the instance_create intent (L0-ENC-23): `access/instance_create` on `access.party:[hex(party)]`, the payload digest in `opaque["payload"]`, validity `valid_from`..`valid_until`.
Digest of the party_register intent (L0-ENC-23): `access/party_register` on `access.party:[hex(party)]`, the payload digest in `opaque["payload"]`, validity `valid_from`..`valid_until`.

basis.description: The Genesis bootstrap Grant the Exercises name as `public` basis (L0-META-7).

pep.description: The PEP the AIS addresses: the identity plane.

party.description: The product's system Party in the domain, 16 bytes; new until its party_register commits.

kid.description: RFC 7638 thumbprint of the registered service key (CR-24).

challenge.description: 32 bytes: the instance_create nonce; party_register uses it followed by 0x01 (OP-149 m.17b (e)).

valid_from.description: RFC 3339: start of the intents' validity.

valid_until.description: RFC 3339: end of it; the challenge is not accepted later.

ais.description: AIS (tagged COSE_Sign1) by the service key over the instance_create intent: nonce the challenge, mode commit, capacity own, the challenge's domain, basis and pep.

register_ais.description: AIS by the service key over the party_register intent (the Party roots itself, actor kind system); exactly when the challenge names party_register.

event_stream.description: The client's SSF push stream to its `suiss_event_receiver`, opened on its first pairing; the same for every tenant (OP-149 m.17 (e)).

PlatformStream.description: An SSF 1.0 §8.1.1 stream configuration with `status`; its schema is `sdks/openapi/events/stream.schema.json`. At creation a webhook stream also carries its `secret` and a poll stream its `access_token`, shown once.

status.description: SSF 1.0 §8.1.2: `disabled` has ended the stream; its row stays (OP-73).

stream_id.description: The stream; the same as the path.

status.description: The new status (SSF 1.0 §8.1.2.2). `disabled` ends the stream for good.

custody.description: No custodial key exists (SI-13, OP-150 m.3 (e)).

binding_key_scope.description: One binding key per domain (CR-18, MD-6).

hsm_partition_shared.description: Whether the HSM partition is shared (CR-30, RT12); null while undeclared.

identity_kms.description: The identity plane has its own token and KEK (T31).

quota_use.description: The signers spend the quota on key generation and unwrap, never per signature (CR-22).

quota_per_second.description: Operations per second the KMS/HSM grants; null while undeclared.

shared.description: Whether the quota is shared with other domains or tenants (HL-20); null while undeclared.

carrier.description: How the Claim arrived (§10.1.2). `unsigned` is an `unsigned-claim` whose channel is the caller's own client certificate: a PEP fact (L2-CLM-5).

claim.description: The Claim as received: a COSE_Sign1 (`application/access-claim+cbor`) or an `unsigned-claim`, CBOR.

body.description: The body beside it when its class has one (`claim-body-binding`, L2-CLB-1); omitted, the Claim stays digest-valued.

evidence.description: SHA-256 of the raw carrier artefact kept in the PII vault; never the artefact.

reason.description: Why a quarantined Claim is held (L2-CLM-3).

replayed.description: An earlier submission had already admitted it.

IntrospectionExtensions.description: Members an RFC 7662 answer adds for an authority token (OP-150 m.2, (l)); an inactive token answers `active: false` only.

authorization_details.description: The token's RFC 9396 details: the `kind` (`intent` or `bounds`), the ActionRef type and schema digest, and the Access members.

cnf.description: The key the token is bound to: `jkt` (RFC 9449) or `x5t#S256` (RFC 8705).

jti.description: The SET the receiver was delivered.

context.description: The reader's `check` context (L1-ADP-5…9) with `query`: the intent's action is `access`/`read` and its first resource `access.search` with the path `[kind]`.

from.description: The version the Grants pin now.

to.description: The version to move them to.

policy.description: The restriction policy replaced; absent for a new one.

grant.description: A Grant; its lineage subtree ends with it.

at.description: When, Unix ms; now when absent.

party.description: The reading Party; any other Party gets an empty page (XI-9, XI-22).

key.description: A compromised key's thumbprint; resolved to its Instance now.

fingerprint.description: The exact digest a `schema-definition` Acceptance pins (E10).

accepted_version.description: The version this domain accepts now.

compatibility.description: The publisher's declaration `{from, relation}` (§9.13.4); a Claim, not a mapping in force.

mappings.description: `{digest, action, from_major, to_major, relation, pinned}`: each mapping the declaration carries and whether a live `schema-definition` Acceptance here pins its digest; an unpinned or broadening mapping changes no coverage (PI-19, OP-157 m.3 (r)).

new_actions.description: Not included in delegations whose catalog is pinned (E11).

role.description: `{name, from, to}` for a role move.

pin.description: The pin each `grant.amend` of the move carries.

policy.description: For a policy candidate: the policy replaced.

structural.description: For a policy candidate: the Kernel's structural reading (OP-157 m.3 (b)); a narrowing is CT1 unless the analysis answers anything but narrowing or equivalent.

items.description: Grant

moves.description: The Grants to amend, one Exercise each.

amends.description: The `grant_amend` payload of each move, in the order of `moves` (L1-ADP-17): the Grant's own constraints, requirements and agency kept, the authority set and pin of the new version; the console drafts, shows and signs each as its own Exercise (X20, §8.17.9.8).

expansion.description: What a widening move needs (INV-10): `{tier, joint_root_quorum, delay_s, requirements}`.

items.description: Grant

exposed.description: `{exercise, holder, class, horizon_ms, window_ms, pep, applied_at}`: projections whose contract outlives it; `applied_at` is when its PEP acknowledged applying the revocation, `null` when unknown (E30).

index_lag.description: Positions the derived index is behind.

orphan_tuples.description: Index rows live for an ended Grant (§5.4).

acknowledged.description: `{pep, applied_at, basis}`: PEPs whose authority-state acknowledgement applies the recorded revocation (§9.12.3, E30); a missing PEP is unknown, not unapplied.

allowed_at.description: The position of the allowing decision, as recorded; a report never changes it (EI-10). `null` when the domain allowed no such Exercise, or for a reporter that is not its actor.

attested.description: `{position, claim, reporter, executor, disposition, step, idempotency_key, outcome, evidence, at, conformance}`: each effect_attestation, `outcome` `done`, `not-done` or `unknown` as reported (never truth, INV-18), `conformance` `conforming`, or outside authority as `outside-envelope`, `outside-window` or `no-exercise` (INV-19).

version.description: The version; the latest when absent.

before.description: Only changes recorded before this position; the newest when absent.

items.description: A Grant the job revokes, one Exercise each.

latest.description: The latest version of the name.

digest.description: The digest a Grant pins it by.

reserved.description: Reserved actions of its prefix namespaces it does not name: only a delegation that names one includes it.

catalogs.description: `{namespace, catalog, catalog_version, newer}`: a catalog-pinned prefix ("as of catalog vN") and the actions accepted after it, not included (E11).

action.description: The core meta-action (L0-META-1); the console shows its plain label, never this id.

grant_quorum.description: Contributions the Grant's own requirements ask for.

joint_root_quorum.description: Further `co_root` contributions a joint root needs at CT3 (§13.7.3).

actions.description: Covered meta-actions that are not reserved, one by one; only what it covers.

action.description: The core meta-action (L0-META-1); the console shows its plain label, never this id.

grant_quorum.description: Contributions the Grant's own requirements ask for.

joint_root_quorum.description: Further `co_root` contributions a joint root needs at CT3 (§13.7.3).

reserved.description: Covered reserved meta-actions (`acceptance.*`, `anchor.*`), shown apart: only a pinned Grant that names them covers them.

since.description: The position that opened the holding episode; with `grant` and `holder` it is an ADP `holding` basis.

id.description: The object: an id in base64url, or a role's name; for a key event, the Claim.

class.description: For a key event: the Claim class (U26, SI-13).

aftermath.description: `{grants_ending, projections_open, honoured_until_ms, running_copies, confirmed_applied}` over the job (XI-3).

max_exposure_ms.description: The longest window of any item.

sources.description: `{acceptance, use, issuer: {party}|{foreign}, classes, namespace, since, protected, dependents}`: each live Acceptance by its canonical use; `dependents` is its blast radius, the live Grants that depend on it (§8.17.9.3, INV-15).

partners.description: `{domain, acceptances, ceilings: [{grant, class, actions, resource, until}]}`: each partner domain and the ceilings of the bridging Grants that recognize its authority (§5.13).

catalog_version.description: The catalog version; after the publisher's latest one (E10).

class.description: `opaque`, or what an authority-relevant parameter decides (E12).

classes.description: The class of every declared parameter (§9.13.3).

core_spec_min.description: Lowest core spec version it needs.

context.description: The publisher's `check` context (L1-ADP-5…9): the intent's action is `access`/`publish`, its resource `access.publication` with the path `[namespace]`, and `opaque.package` the digest of `package` (L1-ADP-18). Its AIS makes the publisher known.

domains.description: Where it is offered; each keeps it in its own scope (TN-20).

fingerprint.description: The exact digest a `schema-definition` Acceptance pins (E10).

publisher.description: The publisher Party: the actor of the AIS.

new.description: Kept now; `false` when every domain already had this exact package.

new_actions.description: Not included in delegations whose catalog is pinned (E11).

suggestion.description: The parameter type to map it to.

warnings.description: Authority-relevant parameters without a closed type (E12); nothing was kept.

groups.description: The groups it shows in (§8.17.7.1); never empty: every Grant the reader gave shows in at least one (XI-10).

source.description: `{anchor}` or `{grant, holder}`: where it derives from.

budget.description: Its authority limits (XI-14); a financial limit is another owner's row.

ref.description: The CommitmentRef digest the holding ends with ("Ends with Work commitment X", §8.17.7.2).

state.description: `active` while the coordinator's current Claim says so, `lapsed` until one does, `ended` for good once it said the commitment ended (EI-5).

selection.description: For a rule-shaped holder the reader was ever selected by, from the membership episode (XI-15, C13, INV-31): `current` and `stale` (the episode is open; an exercise asks for a fresher statement, never "removed") carry the episode's first position `since`, so a rejoin shows its new episode; `ended` (a cutoff, a disqualifying statement or an expired membership Claim) carries the closing position `pos` and time `at` when known. `by` and `stated_at` name the statement behind it, the explanation's second part.

by.description: Who says so (XI-15, §8.17.5.7): the issuer Party of the statement that selects the reader, or of the last one that did when `ended`.

stated_at.description: When that statement was made, Unix ms.

sole.description: Whether the reader is its sole root (§13.8).

by_viewer.description: The reader acted; otherwise someone acted for the reader.

highest.description: The highest incarnation any admitted `resource_lifecycle` Claim named; a create or reincarnate must go above it. `null` when none was declared.

facts.description: `{incarnation, event, claim, issuer, position}` in record order; `event` `create`, `delete` or `reincarnate`.

app.description: The application's client id in the connected service.

name.description: Its display name, when a connector gave one.

registered.description: Whether a live agent or system Party of the domain accounts for it.
